statements.text: Every task the API serializes carries an integer version field, named `version` in JSON.
`POST /tasks` returns HTTP 201 with a task whose `version` is 1.
Tasks seeded at store construction start at `version` 1.
Every successful `PUT /tasks/{id}` increments that task's `version` by exactly 1 (1 -> 2 -> 3 ...).
`UpdateTaskRequest` accepts an OPTIONAL integer field `expectedVersion`; a request body that omits it is still valid and still binds.
When `expectedVersion` is provided and does NOT equal the task's current `version`, `PUT /tasks/{id}` is rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict.
A 409-rejected update leaves the task entirely unchanged: no field is updated and `version` is not bumped.
When `expectedVersion` is provided and MATCHES the current `version`, the update succeeds with HTTP 200 and `version` increments.
When `expectedVersion` is omitted (null), the update proceeds unconditionally (backward-compatible last-writer-wins) with HTTP 200 and `version` increments.
`PUT /tasks/{id}` for an id that does not exist still returns HTTP 404 Not Found, whatever `expectedVersion` carries.
Blank-title validation is unchanged: `POST /tasks` and `PUT /tasks/{id}` with a blank title still return HTTP 400 Bad Request.

`GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}` and `DELETE /tasks/{id}` keep their existing behaviour apart from the added `version` field; the pre-existing 5-test baseline stays green and `dotnet build` stays clean (R-003).
`src/TaskTracker.Api/Domain/**` references no `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*` or endpoint type (R-004), and the `TaskState` naming is preserved (R-005).
